Section B
Answer any three questions.
Each question is introduced by stimulus material. In your answer you may refer to this material and/or
to other examples that you have studied.

parts.label: (a)
parts.text: State two components of the current account.

parts.label: (b)
parts.text: Explain why inflation may fall even if there is an increase in total demand.

parts.label: (c)
parts.text:
Analyse how a country’s current account deficit might be reduced if its firms become
internationally competitive.

parts.label: (d)
parts.text: Discuss whether or not lower taxes on firms will be beneficial for an economy.

text: The election of a new president in South Africa in 2018 led to improvement in business and
consumer confidence. Inflation rates fell despite a rise in total demand. One government policy
measure established areas known as economic zones where firms pay lower, or no, taxes. These
zones encourage domestic firms to become internationally competitive which could reduce the
deficit on the current account of South Africa’s balance of payment.

parts.label: (a)
parts.text: State two sectors, other than the primary sector, in an economy.

parts.label: (b)
parts.text: Explain two possible reasons for a fall in the price of a product such as natural rubber.

parts.label: (c)
parts.text: Analyse the influences on spending.

parts.label: (d)
parts.text: Discuss whether or not the growth of the primary sector is beneficial to a country.

text: Among the reasons for Malaysia’s continued economic growth are rises in consumer spending
and the country’s ability to adapt to changes in global demand. For example, when the price of
natural rubber fell, most rubber plantations changed to palm oil production. The government has
tried to promote the growth of different sectors, including the primary sector.

parts.label: (b)
parts.text: Explain two non-tariff methods of protection.

parts.label: (c)
parts.text:
Analyse, using a production possibility curve (PPC) diagram, the beneficial effects for a
country of the growth of its small and medium-sized firms.

parts.label: (d)
parts.text: Discuss whether or not increased international trade can promote economic growth.

text: South east Asian countries have reduced tariffs between themselves through the ASEAN Free
Trade Agreement. ASEAN member countries are also removing non-tariff methods of protection.
The intention is to raise economic growth through more international trade. This should enable
small and medium-sized firms in ASEAN countries to grow and increase their exports.
